## Image-review calibration

- Work OS `0c699ca1-d4f2-411d-872c-2d9b442920ee`; worktree
  `/home/maigreeks/projects/.worktrees/launchloom-image-review-calibration`,
  branch `codex/launchloom-image-review-calibration`, base `dbdbdd0f`.
- Problem: the v1 reviewer blocked genuine generator defects (fake interfaces,
  headlines, logos) but judged relevance from the business kind alone. It
  approved a generic craft still life as architecture, rejected an image for
  any incidental lettering, and dropped `people_or_faces` from recorded
  reason codes even though the low-level reviewer returned it.
- Implemented `scripts/image-review-policy.mjs` (`visual-review-v2`): the
  intended scene is part of the review, prominent-only text, people policy per
  business kind, stable reason codes, targeted retry directives, and review
  session keys that include the policy and scene so a cached v1 verdict cannot
  be replayed for a changed contract.
- Wired into `scripts/generate-contextual-assets.mjs`: the reviewer receives the
  generation prompt, the retry carries the actual rejection reasons, and skipped
  evidence keeps every reason code.
- Tests: 51 passed across `contextual-assets` and `image-review-policy`;
  `npm run check` reported 0 errors and 0 warnings. A bounded calibration run
  is generating six images across architecture and restaurant cues, plus
  re-reviewing two prior accepted images. Verdicts are not treated as settled
  until the images are inspected.

### Calibration conclusions

- The intended text relaxation works: a small incidental label passes while a
  headline and an interface panel still fail. The interface panel is rejected
  through four independent signals, so the conservative core is intact.
- Approved images were inspected: three architecture interiors, a material
  sample still life, and two restaurant food still lifes. All were relevant;
  none contained readable copy, UI, or branding.
- The rejected restaurant hero was not inspectable because rejected bytes are
  not persisted. A fresh generation of the same scene was approved, so the
  rejection is not evidence of a systematic false positive.
- The niche people policy is reaching the model: the forbid policy produced
  `people_or_faces`. The incidental allowance is not yet proven, because the
  crude composite failed the scene check instead of the people check.
- Main remaining risk is reliability, not strictness: two of twelve reviews
  returned `review_unavailable` (malformed/unavailable provider output). In
  production that skips the image after the bounded retries. That needs a
  separate fix; it is not a threshold calibration issue.

## Image-led delivery guard and reviewer recovery

- Work OS `9f051be3-1518-4fe8-b6e3-8fca714b8709`; worktree
  `/home/maigreeks/projects/.worktrees/launchloom-image-delivery-guard`,
  branch `codex/launchloom-image-delivery-guard`, base `8f3f9e91`.
- Problem: #314 delivered a media-led hero with no approved image because all
  three route images were rejected. The bakeoff recorded the media region but
  not whether it contained raster media, so the preview could still be called
  clean. Separately, the reviewer's third failure mode was an unavailable
  verdict, which skips a usable image.
- Fix: bakeoff evidence now records `heroMediaRegionCount` and
  `heroMediaVisualCount`; the preview validator warns instead of clean when a
  media-led composition rendered no imagery, and warns for missing required
  hero coverage. Reviewer retries now run three times with a distinct review
  session per attempt, and each manifest records `reviewStats`
  (approved/rejected/unavailable) for measurement.
- Tests: 48 passed across the coverage guard and contextual-asset suites;
  type check result recorded in the release log. A live preview after merge
  will confirm the guard fires on a real rejection and that reviewStats is
  populated.
